slides.title: What are they and what is the point?

transcription.tex: A Cartesian equation relates \(x\) and \(y\), for example \(x^2-y^2=5\).\par Parametric equations express both coordinates using another variable, such as \(x=\sin t,\ y=t^2\).\par Each allowed value of \(t\) gives a point on the curve. Eliminating \(t\) does not always preserve the full domain or direction.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Sketching a spiral}\par \(x=\theta\cos\theta,\quad y=\theta\sin\theta,\quad0\le\theta\le4\pi\).\par Mark the points for \(\theta=0,\pi/2,\pi,3\pi/2,2\pi\). What happens during the second turn?
The distance from the origin is \(\theta\). The curve winds anticlockwise outwards, completing two turns. Inverse cosine alone cannot give a single Cartesian description of all turns.

transcription.tex: Show that the line \(y=2x-5\) does not intersect \(x=2t,\ y=4t(t-1)\).
\[4t(t-1)=4t-5\Rightarrow4t^2-8t+5=0\]\[\Delta=64-80=-16<0\]There is no real value of \(t\), so no intersection.

Give parametric equations when \(v=50\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par c. Find its height after 10 seconds and a Cartesian equation. Comment on the model.
\[y(10)=\frac{500}{\sqrt{26}}\approx98.1\text{ m},\quad y=x/5\]Continuing the straight climb indefinitely is unrealistic.

transcription.tex: 2. A descending plane is modelled by \(x=80t,\ y=3000-9.1t\), with distances in metres and \(t\) in minutes.\par a. Find its initial height.\par b. Discuss the stated domain \(0\le t\le329\).\par c. Find the horizontal distance at landing.

\[y=0\Rightarrow t=3000/9.1\approx329.67\]The stated upper bound 329 stops just before landing (height 6.1 m). The exact landing domain ends at \(30000/91\); beyond that the model predicts negative height.

transcription.tex: 3. A ball is kicked from the ground at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), angle \(30^\circ\). Its path is \(x=10\sqrt3t,\ y=10t-4.9t^2\).\par a. Find its horizontal range.\par b. Find when it is descending between heights 1.5 m and 2.5 m.\par c. Find the nearest point where a player can head it in that interval.
\[t_h=\frac{10+\sqrt{100-19.6h}}{9.8}\]Use the larger root for descent: \(t_{2.5}\le t\le t_{1.5}\), approximately \(1.75\le t\le1.88\) s.
